title: A probabilistic interpretation for interpolation Macdonald polynomials
summary: Previous work of Ayyer, Martin, and Williams gave a probabilistic interpretation of the Macdonald polynomials $P_λ(x_1,\dots,x_n;1,t)$ at $q=1$ in terms of a Markov chain called the multispecies $t$-Push TASEP, a Markov chain involving particles of types $λ_1,\dots,λ_n$ hopping around a ring. In particular, they showed that for each composition $η$ obtained by permuting the parts of $λ$, the stationary probability of being in state $η$ is proportional to the ASEP polynomial $F_η(x_1,\dots,x_n; 1,t)$, and the normalizing constant (or partition function) is $P_λ(x_1,\dots,x_n; 1,t)$.
